newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila's Macondray says 1996 net up 63 percent.
newsitem.headline: Manila's Macondray says 1996 net up 63 percent.

text.p: Holding company Macondray and Company Inc (MCI) said on Monday it made a net income of 175 million pesos in 1996, a 63 percent jump from 107 million pesos in 1995.
Its consolidated revenues in 1996 amounted to 5.8 billion pesos, a 314 percent increase from 1.4 billion pesos in 1995.

MCI president and chief executive officer Martin Lorenzo said in a statement the company's 1996 performance reflected the results of its investments in food, consumer finance, packaging and distribution.
The bulk of the 1996 revenues came from newly-acquired Del Monte Pacific Resources Ltd (DMPRL) in a partnership with European-based Del Monte Group Ltd.
DMPRL used to be a unit of South Africa's Del Monte Royal Holdings.
DMPRL posted a net income of 415.1 million pesos in 1996 from revenues of 4.2 billion pesos.

In March 1996, MCI purchased controlling interest of DMPRL. This gave MCI management control of Del Monte Philippines Inc which operates the world's largest pineapple plantation covering 17,000 hectares in Bukidnon province in southern Philippines.

"We intend to sustain MCI's growth and excellent performance...we have put certain plans in place to achieve our budgeted net income of 620 million pesos or an increase of about 250 percent for 1997," Lorenzo said.

Last year, the Philippine Securities and Exchange Commission approved MCI's proposal to sell 91 to 109.2 million shares in a private placement at a price ranging from 12.00 pesos to 14.39 pesos per share.
In its approval, the SEC set a condition that Macondray go public within 1997, unless market conditions does not warrant such undertaking. - Manila newsroom (632) 841-8937
